notes:
Current status: Stalled — technical evaluation flagged major latency risk. Customer ran a day-long POC on our dedicated stack last month; observed persistent p95 spikes on real traffic (10s of seconds during peak). Streaming responses often arrive in fragmented packets, front-end reassembly causes additional 200-500ms overhead per chunk.

Customer quotes: "We can’t ship a generative assistant if p95 is unpredictable — it breaks UX and SLA with partners."

Key signals: engineering team engaged early (SEs built a custom test harness), but after two weeks the internal sponsor (VP Eng) paused decision citing a company-wide hiring/budget freeze. Meanwhile procurement has held on vendor selection pending security sign-off for on-prem deployment. Security wants full audit log retention + KMS integration + air-gapped options for EU data.

Competitive pressure: During freeze, them evaluating BeamScale AI — claims a streaming SDK with lower latency and an EU on-prem appliance. Sales heard customer mention price advantage (~20%) and a faster timeline.

Why stalled: 1) p95 latency not meeting their SLO (target 300-500ms p95 for chat; POC showed 1.2-3s p95 under realistic workload). 2) Streaming chunk fragmentation + front-end work required. 3) Security insists on on-prem/VPC & auditing; we offered Private but timeline uncertain. 4) Internal champion deprioritized due to budget freeze.

Current risk: High. Without a short perf remediation plan or an on-prem pilot that replicates their traffic pattern, likely to go closed-lost.

Suggested playbook (internal): run isolated on-prem micro-benchmark with HLI packet traces (Marcus/SE to schedule), engage infra partner to propose kernel/config tweaks, propose interim UX mitigation (client-side optimistic typing + lower chunk size), and a one-month credit for further testing. If security block persists, offer expanded audit log demo + KMS integration roadmap.

Contact cadence: Tried re-engage via email 2026-03-02 (no reply), left voicemail 2026-03-05. Last substantive call 2026-02-18 (see ff_2026-02-18_0940).
